The application offered benefits to exam performance and student perceived 
engagement levels despite the observed increased levels of distractibility. 
Suggesting that while gamification and short-from content may be more 
distracting, they are also more engaging and effective in education 
environments. 
In retrospect, the project may have been more streamlined, by focusing more 
on immediate gratification systems, which are quicker and simpler to implement, 
and their performance would have been more measurable given the projects 
time constraints. While the analysis may have benefited from a greater focus on 
user interactions, and gauging when students become disengaged during a 
lesson; this would likely create more valuable and actionable insights based on 
student engagement and learning outcomes. 
6.2 Future work 
This project opens several avenues for further expansion and novel research, 
that could significantly enhance educational outcomes. The following proposals 
aim to build on the success and findings from this work and build upon the 
limitations observed during the various stages. 
While this project has integrated spaced repetition and gamified elements, there 
is still incredible potential in adding adaptive learning systems and algorithms. 
This may involve not only adjusting times between revisiting lessons (Tabibian, 
et al., 2019), but adapting the educational content and difficulty based on real-
time data from the students’ performance and engagement; actively attempting 
to increase user retention rates. Developing an adaptive learning system has the 
potential to upend the education system, and significantly bolster student 
engagement and their learning outcomes.
